investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or allocatable count at zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~127–146 seconds across all three checks, no VM was ever assigned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended resource allocatable count is at or near zero, likely because existing remote-agent VMs are consuming all available peer-pod slots and have not been released.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are resource-exhausted; if the selector was recently narrowed or node labels changed, previously schedulable nodes may now be excluded.

TERTIARY — cluster capacity regression: the 6-node cluster may have lost one or more kata-capable nodes (e.g., node eviction, maintenance cordon, or scale-down), reducing the pool of nodes that can satisfy kata.peerpods.io/vm requests.

QUATERNARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user sessions may have created VMs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the resource without active workloads.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 339 > max 300)
investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 339 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the staleness of the published snapshot artifact rather than any broader website or infrastructure outage.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run (or did not successfully publish) within the 300-minute freshness window required by the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482). The snapshot was last published approximately 339 minutes before the eval ran at 2026-07-02T18:11:40.567Z, meaning the workflow was overdue by at least 39 minutes. This is an eval-detected staleness condition scoped to the snapshot publishing pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing website outage is present.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 339' — the single violated assertion is the snapshotAgeMinutes max:300 contract (evidenceItems: failed-check.message, failed-check.evidence).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=339, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — all other assertions passed; only the age threshold was breached (evidenceItem: failed-check.evidence).

expected-output.contract: infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 asserts { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } — this is the exact assertion that failed (evidenceItem: expected-output.contract, source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:474-482).

sibling checks public-observability-page, public-models-page, and public-marketing-pages all passed with HTTP 200 responses, confirming the public website itself is reachable and the failure is isolated to the snapshot artifact (evidenceItems: sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages).

source='github-actions' in the snapshot evidence confirms the snapshot is expected to be produced by a GitHub Actions workflow, making a missed or failed workflow run the primary candidate for the staleness (evidenceItem: failed-check.evidence).

The registry check config at infra/evals/status/features.json line 383 sets staleAfterMinutes:360 for the feature registry, but the expected-output contract enforces a stricter max of 300 minutes — the contract boundary is the one violated (evidenceItem: source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383, source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:379-387).
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot did not execute or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot stale by at least 39 minutes.

Second: The workflow ran but failed to publish the updated snapshot to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json (e.g., a Pages deployment step failed silently), so the file on disk was not updated despite a workflow run.
Third: The workflow schedule was modified, delayed, or the workflow was manually disabled, causing the run cadence to exceed the 300-minute freshness window.
Fourth: A GitHub Actions runner or Pages infrastructure issue caused the workflow to queue but not complete in time, resulting in the snapshot not being refreshed.

Fifth (lower confidence): There is a discrepancy between the registry's staleAfterMinutes:360 and the contract's max:300 — if the workflow is scheduled to run at an interval between 300 and 360 minutes, it would pass the registry staleness check but fail the expected-output contract assertion. This configuration mismatch could cause intermittent eval failures even when the workflow runs on schedule.
